questions.0.question.back: In the past, why did towns often grow where boats stopped on a river?
questions.0.question.source: Long ago, why did towns often grow at places where boats stopped on a river?

questions.0.options.0.text.back: Boats kept the river from flooding
questions.0.options.0.text.source: Boats kept the river from flooding

questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Boats can't stop a river flooding. Towns grew where boats stopped because people could trade there. Look at Lesson 10 again.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Boats cannot stop a river from flooding. Towns grew where boats stopped because people could trade there. Look back at Lesson 10.

questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Right. Boats carried heavy goods, like grain and wood. People bought and sold these goods where the boats stopped.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Boats carried heavy goods, like grain and wood. People bought and sold these goods where the boats stopped.

questions.1.stimulus.items.0.back: River Site: flat land by the river. The soil is good for food crops. Sometimes the river floods this land.
questions.1.stimulus.items.0.source: River site: flat land by the river. The soil is good for crops. Sometimes the river floods it.

questions.1.stimulus.items.1.back: Hill Site: high, dry land. Floods don't reach there. The soil is thin and rocky.
questions.1.stimulus.items.1.source: Hill site: high, dry ground. Floods do not reach it. The soil is thin and rocky.

questions.1.stimulus.items.2.back: Forest Site: far from the river. There is wood for building. People have to cut down trees before farming.
questions.1.stimulus.items.2.source: Forest site: far from the river. There is wood to build with. People must cut trees before they farm.

questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Floods don't reach Hill Site. But the river sometimes floods River Site. Look at Lesson 10 again.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Floods do not reach the Hill site. But the river sometimes floods the River site. Look back at Lesson 10.

questions.1.options.2.text.back: There is wood for building there.

questions.4.question.back: Nairobi and Shenzhen are two real cities. What helped both grow?
questions.4.question.source: Nairobi and Shenzhen are two real cities. What helped both of them grow?

questions.4.options.0.text.back: Cool weather and lots of rain
questions.4.options.0.text.source: Cool weather and lots of rain

questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Weather did not make these two cities grow. Nairobi started as a stopping place on a railway line, and Shenzhen grew when factories opened. Look at Lesson 12 again.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Weather did not make these two cities grow. Nairobi began as a stop on a railway, and Shenzhen grew when factories opened. Look back at Lesson 12.

questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Fertile soil helps fields grow crops. These two cities grew because of jobs and transport. Look at Lesson 12 again.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Rich soil helps farms grow crops. These two cities grew because of jobs and transport. Look back at Lesson 12.

questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Right. Nairobi started as a stopping place on a railway line, and factories opened in Shenzhen. Jobs and transport brought many people.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Nairobi began as a stop on a railway, and factories opened in Shenzhen. Jobs and transport brought many people.

questions.5.stimulus.body.back: A new railway line opened in the fictional town of Ostrin. A factory opened next to the station, with 600 new jobs. Five years later, Ostrin's population doubled. But the town still only had one small school.
questions.5.stimulus.body.source: A new train line opens in the made-up town of Ostrin. A factory opens next to the station, with 600 new jobs. Five years later, twice as many people live in Ostrin. But the town still has only one small school.

questions.5.question.back: What problem is Ostrin most likely to have?

questions.5.options.0.text.back: The only school gets very full.

questions.5.options.1.text.back: Jobs in the town went down.

questions.6.options.1.text.back: Today a cool wind is blowing.
questions.6.options.1.text.source: A cool wind is blowing today.

questions.6.options.1.feedback.back: Right. This is about one day, and it can change quickly. So this is weather.
questions.6.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. This is about one day, and it can change fast. That makes it weather.

questions.6.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. This is what usually happens every year, so this is climate. Weather is the state of the air right now. Look at Lesson 13 again.
questions.6.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. This is what usually happens each year, so it is climate. Weather is what the air is like now. Look back at Lesson 13.
